title: Broad Classification of Industrial Occupancies into Different Degree of Fire Hazard
extraction_confidence_note: Annex B is a 3-column table (G-1 Low / G-2 Moderate / G-3 High) spanning several pages in the source. Text extraction of multi-column tables can shuffle which column a given occupancy name belongs to, especially where a cell wraps across page breaks. The lists below were reconstructed by reading the extracted text in column order but have NOT been cross-checked cell-by-cell against the original table layout. Treat this file as a strong first draft; before using it in production classification logic (especially at a G-1/G-2 boundary that affects the applicability-threshold logic), verify each entry against the source document's actual table.
usage_note: This Annex covers 'fire hazard only' classification. It does not address chemical hazard, pollution, or other regulatory classifications - those should be checked against the relevant state/central guidelines separately. Any occupancy not covered here should be classified in the most appropriate class by resemblance to the proposed occupancy. Where a complex has separate plants of varying hazard degree, consult the Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) on the level of protection to provide.
g1_low_hazard_examples: Asbestos steam packing and lagging manufacturing
Automobiles and other motor vehicles (manufacturing, non-battery)
Cement factories / asbestos or concrete products manufacturing
Ceramic factories and crockery/stoneware pipe manufacturing
Condensed milk factories, milk pasteurizing plant, dairies
Incandescent and fluorescent and TV picture tube manufacturing
Godowns and warehouses storing non-combustible goods only
Water treatment/filtration plants and water pump houses
g2_moderate_hazard_examples: Auto components (excl. plastics and foam) manufacturing
Bookbinders, envelopes and paper bag manufacturing
Carpenters, wood wool and furniture manufacturing
Chemical manufacturing (raw materials with flash point above 23 C)
Cinema films and TV production studios
Coal and/or coke and/or charcoal ball and briquettes manufacturing
Cotton seed cleaning or de-linting factories
Electric generating stations (other than underground power houses)
Godowns and warehouses (other than light/high hazard categories)
Hosiery, lace, embroidery and thread factories
Kitchen with any type of fuel (live cooking)
Manure and fertilizer works (blending, mixing, granulating)
Oil terminals/depots (other than high hazard A)
Open storage of flammable liquids in drums/cans etc.
Paper and cardboard mills without raw material yards
Piers, wharves, jetties and dockyards (other than high hazard A)

sub_category_a: Auto components (including plastics and foam components)
Automobiles and other motor vehicles powered by lithium/lithium-ion batteries manufacturing
Bituminized paper and/or hessian cloth/tar felt manufacturing
Chemical manufacturing (raw materials with flash point below 23 C)
Foam plastics manufacturing and/or converting plants
Grass, hay, fodder and bhoosa (chaff) pressing factories
Industrial gas manufacturing (other than inert/halogenated hydrocarbon gases)
Metal or tin printers (>50 percent floor area as engineering workshop may be taken as Ordinary Hazard Risk)
Oil fire boiler room/oil quenching tank
Oil terminals/depots handling flammable liquids with flash point <=23 C
Paper and cardboard mills with raw material yards
Piers, wharfs and jetties handling extra hazardous materials
Rosin lamp black and turpentine factories
g3_high_hazard_examples.sub_category_b_note: NOTE from source: 'In case of complexes having separate plants having varying degrees of hazard, authority having jurisdiction should be consulted to decide on level of protection to be provided.'
